sections.value:
**Performance: block** at `011eb97664562a2acc980f53161f0a97a6056593`. **P156-F001 closed; new P156-F002 below.**

Delta `a7a0f4a..011eb97`: own fixes b6d9407b/10065a5b and already-reviewed main merges (#155, #136, #153). Source plus exact-head CI only.

## P156-F001 closed: strictly no-launch capture

The detector now calls capture_without_launch. Production routes only to query_live -> ask(may_start=false), returns None rather than starting/replacing/forking a client, and never calls the generic stdout/run fallback. The port default also returns None. A live client gets one visible-screen read per candidate; with no client the candidate is skipped and not told.

CI executes the **real-tmux cold/lost/disabled/warm test**, including a warm-start positive control for its launch instrument, and the daemon test of recorded per-candidate skip with no tell. This is the missing production-path proof, not just FakeTmux counts.

## P156-F002: retry cap depends on successful post-attempt persistence

`modal_stall.rs:235-263` performs wake_pa first, then records either failure count or told. A recording error is only logged. `ModalStall::owes` (`core/modal_stall.rs:79`) checks the persisted told/failed data loaded next round; no attempt reservation or other fallback cap precedes sending.

If record_modal_stall_failure errors while reads continue working, the next round sees the old count and tries again. **One lost update already permits more than five actual failures; repeated lost updates leave attempts uncapped.** Failed told persistence similarly leaves the target owed. Stable message IDs dedupe delivery records, not retry calls, scope/permission work or failed attempts.

This is a source/dataflow finding, not a locally injected store failure. The passing bound regression injects notification errors but keeps counter writes healthy; it checks five persisted failures per recipient, not failure of the bounding instrument.

**Required:** reserve/count an attempt durably before the notification effect, refusing/deferring that attempt when admission cannot persist, or provide another failure-safe cap covering retries and restart. Keep stable IDs and per-recipient success suppression. Add a CI case where the failure/told update fails while reads work; actual notification attempts must remain bounded, not merely the stored count. Pointer sent to Bobcat.

## Per-round cost

Let W supported working/paned/untombstoned seats, C silent candidates, M retained stall rows, and T recipient metadata within a stretch.

- **Healthy/no candidate:** one latest_matching API call per W, **four indexed per-kind SELECTs in a read snapshot**, schema/transaction overhead and up to four event payload decodes. Zero capture calls with C=0. At 60 s, four SELECTs are about **0.067/s per eligible seat**.
- **Candidate:** one capture_without_launch call per round, about **0.017 calls/s per candidate** at 60 s. No process for capture, even cold/lost/disabled. Whole visible pane bytes are read; the former post-read 500-row truncation is no longer used. Matching is fixed-marker linear screen work, with fixed labels rather than copied first-line content.
- **Control unavailable:** zero capture output/tells, but **one attempted watchdog.round skip publication per candidate**, with its SQLite/task/broadcast cost. Zero launches is not zero I/O.
- **Inventory:** first successful candidate read fetches all M latest-per-seat records, including history, and each candidate scans the vector; O(M+C*M) remains. A found record is cloned, including told/failed collections. Views also parse this metadata even when only a label is rendered; no new inventory/churn cardinality cap.
- **Targets/retries:** every matched candidate resolves current parent/PA/prime, even when previous targets are already told or exhausted. This reuses scope/roster/ancestry and possible cached-placement Git work; no-tell does not skip target discovery. At most two distinct targets are tried per candidate per round. Under healthy persistence, each target gets at most five failures and successful targets stop; a new PA is a new target/budget, not a global five per stall. F002 prevents certifying that cap under persistence failure.
- **Writes:** new stretch UPSERT; open-state toggles as needed; one failure-count or told UPDATE transaction per attempted target; one modal audit when attempts occurred. JSON collection work/storage follows recipient count/bytes. No separate retry timer: it rides the existing round.

quiet_seq/sequence re-arm is fixed-size metadata; timestamps now only price duration. Schema 40 includes 0039 and amended unmerged 0040, above main 39. Existing global publication/SQL waits and synchronous control reply waits still add round latency.

**CI:** CLEAN at this exact head. [CI 42390021868](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42390021868) succeeds in all four jobs: **2,129 executed Rust cases, zero failures/errors**, five skips separately. JUnit confirms strict capture, per-candidate recorded skip, retry/success/restart/later-target behavior, healthy-store bound, earlier-clock re-arm, fixed-label nonleakage and all six spawn guards. Both visible delivers runs pass, latest **42390652252**. None proves F002's failed budget-write case.

No local build, test, fault trigger, capture, model call or worktree edit. After resolution/deploy, matched capture/skip/tell counts, failure-ledger effectiveness, round latency, CPU/RSS and existing launch-site rates remain owed.
